newsitem.title: UK: Wickes to raise 53.2 mln cash via share issue.
newsitem.headline: Wickes to raise 53.2 mln cash via share issue.

text.p: Troubled British do-it-yourself retailer Wickes Plc, whose former senior managers are under investigation by the Serious Fraud Office, on Thursday announced it would raise 53.2 million pounds via a share issue.
The group, whose shares have been suspended since June when accounting irregularities emerged, also revealed it was in talks for the possible sale of its businesses in continental Europe.

Wickes said the cash call was part of a reorganisation, which included a capital reduction and new banking facilities of 52 million pounds ($86.17 million). These were designed to eliminate the deficit on the firm's profit and loss account.

The company said in a statement: "The directors believe that the group is now in a position where, if the proposals and proposed banking arrangements are implemented, it can build on its market position, return to profitability and deliver a successful "New Wickes'."
The share issue, after the capital reorganisation, will be based on one new share for every one new share held at 150 pence each.

Wickes also published revised accounts for the year to December 31 1995, which showed a loss before tax of 279.3 million pounds, 21.3 million more than originally reported. The group said it expected to make a loss before tax in 1996 of not more than 56 million pounds. It will not pay an interim dividend in 1996 or 1997, but may pay a final dividend in 1997 and an interim for 1998.

Wickes reported that in the nine months to September 28, it notched up a loss of 52.7 million pounds. It predicted that losses for the full year ending December 31 were likely to be not more than 56 million pounds.

The nine-month loss comprises a number of charges. Professional and bank fees, including those for investigating the accounting scandal, were 6.6 million pounds, with UK and continental reorganisation costs of 11 million. The cost of withdrawing from timber operations was put at 13.5 million and interest payments at 4.4 million pounds. ($1=.6056 Pound)
